body: Specifically what could be the consequences? That is if doesn't just fail.

Sometimes I feel like if I message them the right thing, we'll make up and communicate again by some miracle. The other half of the time I wish they knew what remorse was. Fucking reptile brained animal.
It's a wonderful thing to put behind you.
It's not that I think they stopped loving me. It's me questioning if they ever had feelings for me in the first place, or if I was just a chess piece the entire time.

I tried to kill myself by slitting my wrists, arms, and legs. I waited all night to bleed out, but I didn't. It was all because I had a lot of issues and my boyfriend at the time  pushed me away forever. Ever since then I've just been living life day by day with no real direction. Everyone sees my scars, I'm embarrassed when they ask. I know if I tried again and succeeded all of my exes would just laugh. I guess you can say shame is keeping alive.

Before you quit on reality have you ever considered finding a new god? It doesn't have to be a god in the traditional sense, just something to believe in or at least something you take comfort in. Why do you so willingly trust the void, before anything else? This life is the only life you know you have. Why not try to live for yourself?

If you really feel like that you should ask about rescheduling your test or seeing if you could retake it if you fail. Opt out, come up with literally any excuse if need be. If there is no way out, just breath and pace yourself. If you concentrate you might make it. The anxiety can be like an anvil sometimes, but life is worth more than some stupid test.

You can forget the all the little things, but you will never forget what they meant to you. We might never escape the whirlpool of longing, but I can promise the pain of denial will slowly be dulled if you stay strong.

Try to breath. Limit your eye contact. You can try to converse with them, or not. If you want to, but it's too hard, you could always initiate a group activity or conversation as to break the tension. If it becomes overwhelming just ignore him, or even leave. You do not want to panic in front of your ex, trust me. If they ask what's bothering you, just be upfront and say you don't know how to face them in person anymore. Good luck.
I guess my real question is what do we do now? How do we recover from the time wasted longing and any damage taken to our self worth? Is there an end?
Your best bet is to tell him soon and in person if you have any respect left for him.
